prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the best choice depends on your priorities (lowest price, longest warranty, fastest scheduling, brand preference, good reviews, etc.). I can, however, help you pick a top provider and what to look for so you get a reliable replacement.

Quick options to consider
- Manufacturer-authorized dealers (Trane, Carrier, Lennox). These dealers are trained on specific brands and often offer strong warranties.
- Large regional companies with big Atlanta presence (example: Coolray) and national franchise brands that operate locally (Service Experts, One Hour Heating & Air, ARS/Rescue Rooter). These tend to have established service programs and financing options.
- Well-rated local independent contractors — sometimes the best value and service if they’re properly licensed and insured.

How to choose the right company (checklist)
1. Licensing & insurance — contractor and business insurance are required. Ask for license number and verify with the State of Georgia if needed.  
2. References & reviews — check Google, Yelp, BBB and ask the contractor for recent local references.  
3. Technical qualifications — NATE-certified techs and manufacturer certifications are good signs.  
4. Proper sizing — require a Manual J load calculation (not just “match the old tonnage”). Oversized/undersized systems cause problems.  
5. Written, itemized estimate — includes equipment model numbers, SEER rating, if ductwork is included, permit costs, labor warranty, and removal of old equipment.  
6. Permitting & code compliance — contractor should pull city/county permits and schedule inspections if required.  
7. Warranties — look for both parts warranty and a solid labor warranty (ask how long and whether it’s transferable).  
8. Installation quality — ask about line set length, coil compatibility, proper charge (not “factory charge”), and whether they test airflow and refrigerant charge after install.  
9. Financing & rebates — ask about manufacturer, utility, and federal/state rebates, and payment plans.  
10. Post-install support — availability for follow-up service and maintenance plans.

Ballpark cost (Atlanta area, typical central AC replacement)
- Small replacement (straight swap, minimal ductwork): roughly $3,500–$6,000.  
- Mid-range whole-system replacement (good SEER 14–16): $5,500–$9,000.  
- High-efficiency systems, equipment plus ductwork or home-specific upgrades: $8,000–$15,000+.  
(Prices vary by brand, tonnage, complexity and your home — get multiple written quotes.)

Questions to help me give a specific recommendation
- What’s your ZIP code / neighborhood in Atlanta?  
- House type (single-family, multi-family), square footage, age of current system, and whether you need total replacement or just the outdoor unit.  
- Any brand preference or budget target?

If you want, give me your ZIP and a few system details and I’ll list 3–5 well-reviewed HVAC contractors near you and what to ask each when you get quotes.
